title: Review and Fix Cycle Simulator
description: A mock screenshot with three seeded layout defects (clipped row labels, a residual text stroke, a title under a panel), a three-box cycle tracker, a checklist strip and an edit log. For the selected defect the learner chooses the smallest correct patch, an over-broad patch or a wrong-cause patch; each apply re-captures and uses a cycle. After three cycles the simulator locks until Stop and report, whose report scores fixes, new defects and cycles and explains each choice.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Quality Assurance
MicroSim Engineering

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
educational.topic: The smallest patch rule and the fix cycle limit
learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether each proposed patch follows the smallest patch rule and decide when the fix cycle limit requires stopping and reporting.
prerequisites: Layout defects and the fixes table (Chapter 13)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements.

controls.label: Show hint from the fixes catalog

simulation.modelType: Decision simulation with a cycle budget
assumptions: Smallest patches clear only their defect; over-broad patches clear it and add one new defect; wrong-cause patches change nothing.
limitations: Real patches can have partial effects; here each patch has one of three clean outcomes.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judgment under a constraint with explained feedback
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Choice evaluation with a scored report (Evaluate level)
keyQuestions: Does this patch change anything besides the cause of the defect?
If a patch changed nothing, what does that tell you about its cause?
When must the review stop, and what must it report?
commonMisconceptions: A patch that fixes the defect is a good patch.
More cycles always lead to a better result.
Stopping with FAILs left is a failure of the reviewer.
assessmentOpportunities: The learner reaches a clean state in three cycles using only smallest patches.
The learner justifies why each rejected patch is over-broad or aimed at the wrong cause.
